User.title: User
User.description: Represents an application user with defined roles and access. Authentication handled by an external system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: Email address of the user, used for login and communication.

displayName.description: A human-readable name for the user.

role.description: Assigned role of the user (e.g., admin, cashier, warehouse, driver, accountant) determining permissions.

locationId.description: Reference to the primary location associated with this user. (Relationship: Location 1:N User)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

Location.title: Location
Location.description: Represents a physical business location, such as a shop or warehouse, supporting multi-location inventory.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Location entity.

name.description: The name of the location (e.g., 'Main Store', 'Warehouse A').

address.description: The physical address of the location.

phoneNumber.description: Contact phone number for the location.

email.description: Contact email address for the location.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Defines a single product or service available for sale or purchase.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

name.description: The common name of the product.

description.description: A detailed description of the product.

category.description: The category the product belongs to (e.g., 'Electronics', 'Groceries').

unitType.description: The unit of measurement for the product (e.g., 'Pcs', 'Kg', 'Ltr').

sku.description: Stock Keeping Unit, a unique identifier for the product often used internally.

barcode.description: The barcode associated with the product for quick scanning.

minStockAlertQuantity.description: The minimum stock level for this product globally, triggering an alert if quantity falls below it.

purchasePrice.description: The average or last known purchase price of the product.

salePrice.description: The default selling price of the product.

isActive.description: Indicates if the product is currently active and available.

Supplier.title: Supplier
Supplier.description: Represents a company or individual from whom products are purchased.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Supplier entity.

contactPerson.description: The primary contact person at the supplier company.

phoneNumber.description: Contact phone number for the supplier.

email.description: Contact email address for the supplier.

address.description: The physical address of the supplier.

Customer.title: Customer
Customer.description: Represents an individual or business that purchases products from the app.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Customer entity.

phoneNumber.description: Contact phone number for the customer.

email.description: Contact email address for the customer.

address.description: The physical address of the customer.

loyaltyPoints.description: Accumulated loyalty points for the customer, if applicable.

Stock.title: Stock
Stock.description: Tracks the quantity of a specific product available at a particular location.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Stock entity.

productId.description: Reference to the Product entity. (Relationship: Product 1:N Stock)

locationId.description: Reference to the Location entity. (Relationship: Location 1:N Stock)

quantity.description: The current quantity of the product at this location.

lastUpdated.description: Timestamp of the last update to the stock quantity for this product at this location.

minStockQuantity.description: The minimum stock level for this product at THIS location, triggering an alert if quantity falls below it. Overrides product's general minStockAlertQuantity.

PurchaseOrder.title: PurchaseOrder
PurchaseOrder.description: Represents an order placed with a supplier for goods or services.

id.description: Unique identifier for the PurchaseOrder entity.

supplierId.description: Reference to the Supplier entity from whom the order is placed. (Relationship: Supplier 1:N PurchaseOrder)

locationId.description: Reference to the Location where the purchased products are expected to be received. (Relationship: Location 1:N PurchaseOrder)

userId.description: Reference to the User who created or managed this purchase order. (Relationship: User 1:N PurchaseOrder)

orderDate.description: The date when the purchase order was created.

expectedDeliveryDate.description: The anticipated date for the delivery of the ordered items.

actualDeliveryDate.description: The actual date when the ordered items were delivered.

status.description: The current status of the purchase order (e.g., 'Pending', 'Ordered', 'Partially Received', 'Received', 'Cancelled').

totalAmount.description: The total monetary value of the purchase order.

notes.description: Additional notes or comments regarding the purchase order.

PurchaseOrderItem.title: PurchaseOrderItem
PurchaseOrderItem.description: Represents a single line item within a purchase order, detailing a specific product and its ordered quantity.

id.description: Unique identifier for the PurchaseOrderItem entity.

purchaseOrderId.description: Reference to the PurchaseOrder this item belongs to. (Relationship: PurchaseOrder 1:N PurchaseOrderItem)

productId.description: Reference to the Product being ordered. (Relationship: Product 1:N PurchaseOrderItem)

orderedQuantity.description: The quantity of the product ordered.

receivedQuantity.description: The quantity of the product actually received, useful for partial deliveries.

unitPrice.description: The agreed-upon purchase price per unit of the product at the time of order.

totalPrice.description: The total price for this item (ordered quantity * unit price).

SalesOrder.title: SalesOrder
SalesOrder.description: Represents a sale transaction, encompassing POS sales, invoices, and wholesale orders.

id.description: Unique identifier for the SalesOrder entity.

customerId.description: Reference to the Customer making the purchase. Can be null for anonymous or walk-in sales. (Relationship: Customer 1:N SalesOrder)

locationId.description: Reference to the Location where the sale was made. (Relationship: Location 1:N SalesOrder)

userId.description: Reference to the User who processed the sale. (Relationship: User 1:N SalesOrder)

orderType.description: The type of sales order (e.g., 'POS', 'Invoice', 'Wholesale Order').

orderDate.description: The date and time when the sales order was placed/recorded.

status.description: The current status of the sales order (e.g., 'Pending', 'Completed', 'Cancelled', 'Refunded').

subtotalAmount.description: The sum of prices of all items before any discounts or taxes.

discountAmount.description: The total amount of discount applied to the order.

taxAmount.description: The total tax amount applied to the order.

totalAmount.description: The final total amount of the sales order after discounts and taxes.

amountPaid.description: The amount of money already paid towards this sales order, for tracking partial payments.

shippingAddress.description: The shipping address for the order, if applicable.

billingAddress.description: The billing address for the order, if applicable.

notes.description: Additional notes or comments regarding the sales order.

invoiceNumber.description: A unique invoice number generated for this sales order, if applicable.

SalesOrderItem.title: SalesOrderItem
SalesOrderItem.description: Represents a single line item within a sales order, detailing a specific product and its sold quantity.

id.description: Unique identifier for the SalesOrderItem entity.

salesOrderId.description: Reference to the SalesOrder this item belongs to. (Relationship: SalesOrder 1:N SalesOrderItem)

productId.description: Reference to the Product being sold. (Relationship: Product 1:N SalesOrderItem)

quantity.description: The quantity of the product sold in this item.

unitPrice.description: The selling price per unit of the product for this specific order item.

totalPrice.description: The total price for this item (quantity * unit price).

Payment.title: Payment
Payment.description: Tracks payments received from customers, typically against sales orders.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Payment entity.

salesOrderId.description: Reference to the SalesOrder to which this payment is applied. (Relationship: SalesOrder 1:N Payment)

amount.description: The monetary amount of the payment.

paymentDate.description: The date and time when the payment was received/recorded.

transactionReference.description: A reference number for the transaction (e.g., card transaction ID, cheque number).

userId.description: Reference to the User who recorded this payment. (Relationship: User 1:N Payment)

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, matching 'request.auth.uid'.

params.name: locationId
params.description: The unique identifier of the business location.

params.name: productId

params.name: stockItemId
params.description: The unique identifier for the stock item (combination of product and location).

params.name: purchaseOrderId

params.name: purchaseOrderId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent purchase order.

params.name: purchaseOrderItemId
params.description: The unique identifier of the item within the purchase order.

definition.description: Manages sales transactions (POS, invoices, wholesale). Each document explicitly includes `locationId` and `userId` for authorization. Access is controlled by the user's role and their assigned location.

params.name: salesOrderId
params.description: The unique identifier of the sales order.

definition.description: Line items for a specific sales order. For authorization independence, each document *must* also include the `locationId` and `userId` denormalized from its parent `SalesOrder`. This allows rules to evaluate access without needing to `get()` the parent document.

params.name: salesOrderId
params.description: The unique identifier of the parent sales order.

params.name: salesOrderItemId
params.description: The unique identifier of the item within the sales order.

For authorization independence, each document *must* also include the `locationId` denormalized from its associated `SalesOrder`. This facilitates location-based access control and user-specific payment tracking without needing additional `get()` calls.

params.description: The unique identifier of the payment record.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and debuggable by strictly adhering to the core design principles and strategy mandates. 

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL) & QAPs:**

1.  **Denormalization for Authorization Independence:** To eliminate `get()` calls in security rules for checking hierarchical or related document permissions, key authorization fields are denormalized:
    *   `PurchaseOrderItem` documents will include the `locationId` and `userId` from their parent `PurchaseOrder`.
    *   `SalesOrderItem` documents will include the `locationId` and `userId` from their parent `SalesOrder`.
    *   `Payment` documents will include the `locationId` from the `SalesOrder` they pertain to.
    This ensures that any read or write operation on these documents can be authorized solely by examining the document's own data (`resource.data`) and the requesting user's identity (`request.auth.uid`) and their pre-fetched role/location (from their `/users/{uid}` profile, which is a standard, acceptable `get()` for user context).

2.  **Structural Segregation & QAPs for List Operations:**
    *   **User Roles (`/users/{userId}`):** User profiles containing `role` and primary `locationId` are stored at `/users/{userId}`. This path-based ownership makes it easy for users to access their own profiles and for admins to manage them. Security rules will use `get(/users/$(request.auth.uid))` to fetch the user's role and associated location for permission checks across other collections.
    *   **Global, Homogeneous Collections (`/locations`, `/products`, `/suppliers`, `/customers`):** These collections store entities that are generally accessible (read) by various roles within the organization, with write access typically restricted to `admin` or specific `warehouse` / `accountant` roles. Their top-level nature and absence of user-specific ownership simplify `list` queries, which can be protected by checking the user's role.
    *   **Location-Scoped & User-Scoped Collections (`/stock_items`, `/purchase_orders`, `/sales_orders`, `/payments`):** Each document in these collections explicitly contains a `locationId` and/or `userId` field. This design enables secure `list` operations (Query-Appraisal Patterns - QAPs) by allowing security rules to enforce that any `list` query *must* include a `where('locationId', '==', user.locationId)` filter. This prevents users from inadvertently or maliciously querying data outside their authorized location or their own transactions, making the rules robust and preventing accidental data leakage. The `userId` field also facilitates secure queries for a user's own orders/payments.

**Clarity of Intent & Debuggability:**
*   Collection names (e.g., `users`, `purchase_orders`, `stock_items`) are semantic and descriptive. Wildcards are explicit (e.g., `{userId}`, `{purchaseOrderId}`). Authorization fields (`userId`, `locationId`, `status`) are consistently named and explicitly present in documents where needed, making security rules highly readable and easier to debug. Finite State Machine patterns (like `status` fields) provide clear intent.

**DBAC:**
*   User roles and primary location associations are stored directly within the `/users/{userId}` documents, leveraging Firestore for Database Access Control rather than custom claims. This keeps all authorization logic within the database and rules, simplifying management and debugging.

This structure ensures that security rules are straightforward, relying primarily on `request.auth.uid` and `resource.data` fields, augmented by a single `get()` to the user's own profile for contextual roles and location, thereby optimizing for security and performance.
